```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
options(digits = 6, width = 95)
```

This vignette walks one real chamber closure through every step between the
raw 1 Hz record and the number that would be reported in a table, printing every
intermediate value. Nothing here is interactive, so the document can be rebuilt
with `rmarkdown::render()`.

## The closure

`stemflux` ships one closure, `2021-05-18_5086_I_7.0`: a 600 s tree-stem
measurement at Yale-Myers Forest (Connecticut) with a semi-rigid sleeve chamber
and an ABB/LGR micro-portable UGGA logging at 1 Hz. The chamber geometry comes
from the campaign auxfile and is stored by `example_closure()`:

| auxfile column | value | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Area`  | 4254.121 cm2 | stem surface enclosed |
| `Vtot`  | 7.082698 L | chamber + tubing + analyzer cell |
| `Tcham` | 26.02 C | chamber air temperature |
| `Pcham` | 101.325 kPa | pressure |

The archived trace holds dry mole fractions only (no H2O column), so the flux
term is computed with `H2O_ppm = 0`, i.e. no water-vapour correction. That is
the one assumption in this example.

```{r load}
library(stemflux)
d <- example_closure(dead.band = 60)
str(d[, c("UniqueID", "POSIX.time", "t_s", "CO2dry_ppm", "CH4dry_ppb", "flag", "Etime")])
```

```{r raw-plot, fig.height = 5}
op <- par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(3, 4.5, 1.5, 1))
plot(d$t_s, d$CO2dry_ppm, pch = 16, cex = 0.4, col = ifelse(d$flag == 1, "grey20", "grey70"),
     xlab = "", ylab = "CO2 (ppm)", main = "raw closure; grey = dead band")
abline(v = 60, col = "red", lty = 2)
plot(d$t_s, d$CH4dry_ppb, pch = 16, cex = 0.4, col = ifelse(d$flag == 1, "grey20", "grey70"),
     xlab = "seconds since closure", ylab = "CH4 (ppb)")
abline(v = 60, col = "red", lty = 2)
par(op)
```

## Step 1: dead band

The first 60 s after closure are discarded (chamber mixing, operator
disturbance). `example_closure()` already applied this through `flag_window()`;
the rows with `flag == 1` are what every fit below uses.

```{r deadband}
n_total <- nrow(d); n_used <- sum(d$flag == 1)
t_span  <- max(d$Etime[d$flag == 1]) - min(d$Etime[d$flag == 1])
c(n_total = n_total, n_used = n_used, t_span_s = t_span)
```

## Step 2: fitted dC/dt

### 2a. Transparent linear fit

```{r lm}
w <- d[d$flag == 1, ]
fit_ch4 <- lm(CH4dry_ppb ~ Etime, data = w)
fit_co2 <- lm(CO2dry_ppm ~ Etime, data = w)
slope_ch4 <- unname(coef(fit_ch4)[2]); slope_co2 <- unname(coef(fit_co2)[2])
c(CH4_slope_ppb_per_s = slope_ch4, CH4_r2 = summary(fit_ch4)$r.squared,
  CH4_slope_SE = summary(fit_ch4)$coefficients[2, 2])
c(CO2_slope_ppm_per_s = slope_co2, CO2_r2 = summary(fit_co2)$r.squared)
```

### 2b. goFlux linear and Hutchinson-Mosier fits

`goFlux::goFlux()` fits both the linear model (LM) and the non-linear
Hutchinson-Mosier model (HM), and `goFlux::best.flux()` picks one using its
default criteria. goFlux prints a progress bar; it is captured here.

```{r goflux}
invisible(capture.output({
  res_ch4 <- suppressWarnings(goFlux::goFlux(d, "CH4dry_ppb"))
  res_co2 <- suppressWarnings(goFlux::goFlux(d, "CO2dry_ppm"))
}))
best_ch4 <- suppressWarnings(goFlux::best.flux(res_ch4))
best_co2 <- suppressWarnings(goFlux::best.flux(res_co2))
as.data.frame(best_ch4[, c("LM.slope", "LM.r2", "LM.SE", "HM.slope", "HM.r2", "HM.k",
                           "model", "quality.check")])
```

`LM.slope` is the same number as the hand-rolled `lm()` above (`r signif(slope_ch4, 5)` ppb/s).

## Step 3: unit conversion

The gas columns are mole fractions: ppm = umol mol-1, ppb = nmol mol-1. A slope
in ppb s-1 is therefore already in nmol mol-1 s-1; converting to mol mol-1 s-1
is a factor of 1e-9.

```{r units}
slope_ch4_molfrac <- slope_ch4 * 1e-9   # mol mol-1 s-1
slope_co2_molfrac <- slope_co2 * 1e-6
c(CH4 = slope_ch4_molfrac, CO2 = slope_co2_molfrac)
```

## Step 4: V/A and P/RT

```{r geometry}
Area_m2 <- 4254.121 / 1e4
Vtot_m3 <- 7.082698 / 1e3
T_K     <- 26.02 + 273.15
P_Pa    <- 101.325 * 1e3
R       <- 8.314
VA      <- Vtot_m3 / Area_m2          # m
PRT     <- P_Pa / (R * T_K)           # mol m-3 (molar density of air)
c(V_over_A_m = VA, P_over_RT_mol_m3 = PRT, product_mol_m2 = VA * PRT)
```

`flux_term()` is the same product written with goFlux's unit conventions
(litres, kPa, cm2, Celsius):

```{r fluxterm}
ft <- flux_term(V_L = 7.082698, P_kPa = 101.325, A_cm2 = 4254.121, T_C = 26.02)
c(flux_term = ft, goFlux_flux.term = best_ch4$flux.term)
```

## Step 5: flux

```{r flux}
flux_ch4_mol   <- slope_ch4_molfrac * VA * PRT        # mol m-2 s-1
flux_ch4_nmol  <- flux_ch4_mol * 1e9                  # nmol m-2 s-1
flux_co2_umol  <- slope_co2_molfrac * VA * PRT * 1e6  # umol m-2 s-1
c(CH4_flux_nmol_m2_s = flux_ch4_nmol, CO2_flux_umol_m2_s = flux_co2_umol)
# the shortcut used by goFlux: slope in ppb/s times flux.term gives nmol m-2 s-1 directly
c(shortcut = slope_ch4 * ft, goFlux_LM = best_ch4$LM.flux, goFlux_HM = best_ch4$HM.flux,
  goFlux_best = best_ch4$best.flux)
```

## Step 6: per-measurement precision

Instrument noise is estimated from the measurement itself, not the datasheet.
First differences remove the (linear) flux signal; white noise survives with
variance 2 sigma^2, so sigma = SD(diff(x)) / sqrt(2).

```{r precision}
sigma_ch4 <- precision_allan(w$CH4dry_ppb)
sigma_co2 <- precision_allan(w$CO2dry_ppm)
c(sigma_CH4_ppb = sigma_ch4, sigma_CO2_ppm = sigma_co2,
  datasheet_CH4_ppb = 0.9, datasheet_CO2_ppm = 0.35,
  robust_MAD_CH4_ppb = precision_mad(w$CH4dry_ppb))
```

This analyzer was about 2.5 times noisier in CH4 than its datasheet claims,
which is why datasheet precision should not be used for detection limits.

## Step 7: minimum detectable flux by each method, by hand

```{r mdf}
t_used <- max(w$Etime) + 1     # goFlux's t; = nb.obs at 1 Hz
mdf <- mdf_multi(flux.term = ft, t = t_used,
                 prec = 0.9,               # manufacturer, for the goFlux method
                 sigma = sigma_ch4,        # this closure (Christiansen, 2-sigma)
                 sigma.global = sigma_ch4) # a campaign median would go here (Wassmann)
t(round(mdf, 6))
# by hand, Table 2.5 criterion: (2 sigma / t) (V/A) (P/RT)
c(MDF_2sigma_by_hand = (2 * sigma_ch4 * 1e-9 / t_used) * VA * PRT * 1e9)
```

All MDFs are in nmol m-2 s-1. The regression standard error of the slope
(`LM.SE` = `r signif(best_ch4$LM.SE, 3)` nmol m-2 s-1) is far smaller than any of
them, which is the expected behaviour of these single-sample criteria.

## Step 8: precision, MDF and detection flags with `flag_detection()`

`flag_detection()` does steps 6-7 for every row of a `best.flux()` table, for
every combination of precision estimator and MDF method you ask for, and then
picks *one* combination as the reported `MDF` (the `primary`). Nothing is
deleted; rows are flagged.

```{r flag}
rep_ch4 <- flag_detection(best_ch4, traces = d, gastype = "CH4dry_ppb",
                          precision = c("allan", "mad", "datasheet"),
                          mdf = c("goflux", "wassmann", "christiansen", "two_sigma"),
                          conf = c(0.90, 0.95, 0.99),
                          primary = list(precision = "allan", mdf = "christiansen", conf = 0.95))
t(as.data.frame(rep_ch4[, grep("^sigma_", names(rep_ch4))]))
mdf_cols <- setdiff(grep("^MDF_", names(rep_ch4), value = TRUE), c("MDF_goflux_orig", "MDF_method"))
t(round(as.data.frame(rep_ch4[, mdf_cols]), 6))   # every combination
t(as.data.frame(rep_ch4[, c("MDF", "MDF_method", "below_MDF", "detected", "det_class")]))
```

Column names follow `MDF_<method>_<precision>[_<conf>]`, so
`MDF_christiansen_allan_95` is the Christiansen criterion with this closure's
Allan precision at 95 percent, and `MDF_goflux_datasheet` is goFlux's own MDF.

## Choosing precision and MDF

There is no single right choice; the point of computing several is that the
report can say which one it used and readers can convert. The decision
depends on what the number is for.

**Which precision estimate?**

| estimator | what it is | use when | where it comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| bench sigma (Box 2 of the guidelines paper) | SD of a sealed, spiked or standard-gas run on the *same* analyzer | you ran the bench test; best single number for the instrument | `flag_detection(sigma = ...)` (labelled `custom`) |
| per-closure Allan (`allan`) | SD(diff x)/sqrt(2) on each closure's flagged rows | default; tracks day-to-day analyzer state, cell fouling, temperature | `precision_by_id()`, `flag_detection(precision = "allan")` |
| record-wide MAD (`mad`) | MAD(diff x)/sqrt(2) over a whole record or closure | records with breaths, moves, chamber swaps; robust global number | `precision_mad()`, `flag_detection(precision = "mad")` |
| rolling quietest windows (`rolling`) | median residual SD of the flattest 5 percent of 30-s windows | comparison only; biased low ~20 percent on white noise | `precision_rolling()`, `flag_detection(precision = "rolling")` |
| datasheet (`datasheet`) | manufacturer 1-s precision | never for detection limits on field-worn analyzers (2.5x too optimistic here); kept for comparability with goFlux | `prec` argument of `goFlux::import.*()`, `flag_detection(precision = "datasheet")` |

**Which MDF method?**

| question | recommended | reason |
|---|---|---|
| campaign means, budgets, upscaling | keep every flux; flag with `two_sigma` or `christiansen`; do not delete | removing below-MDF values biases means upward; the flag documents the fraction below detection |
| is this individual flux non-zero? | `christiansen` at a stated confidence (per-measurement sigma, t-quantile) | a per-closure test with the closure's own noise and degrees of freedom |
| comparing with other studies | report all: `goflux` (datasheet), `wassmann` (global, z), `christiansen` (per closure, t), `two_sigma` | each literature uses a different one; the table lets readers convert |
| instrument-level statement ("our system detects X") | `wassmann` with a global sigma (campaign median or bench) | designed as an instrument/protocol limit rather than a per-closure one |

**Where each is set in the pipeline.** The `prec` argument given to
`goFlux::import.*()` (or the `*_prec` columns) only feeds goFlux's own `MDF`
column and the `MDF` criterion inside `best.flux()`. stemflux's estimators are
applied *after* `best.flux()` by `flag_detection()`, which reads the flagged
traces, adds `sigma_*`, `MDF_*` and `below_*` columns, and sets the reported
`MDF`/`below_MDF`/`MDF_method` from `primary`. Nothing is deleted at any step:
`det_class` says `"below detection"`, and the row stays.

## Step 9: quality screens

Physical checks, each an independent flag (`TRUE` = fired), never a deletion.
Is the CO2 tracer positive (the chamber was sealed and respiration
accumulated)? Did the chamber start near ambient? Is the trace convex? Is the
window long enough? With one measurement the C0 screen compares the closure to
itself, so it passes trivially; in a campaign the median is taken over all
closures.

```{r qc}
rep_ch4 <- qc_screens(rep_ch4, traces = d, gastype = "CH4dry_ppb", co2 = best_co2,
                      screens = list(c0 = list(k = 1.5), co2_tracer = list(min_slope = 0),
                                     convex = TRUE, min_window = list(secs = 120)),
                      verbose = FALSE)
t(as.data.frame(rep_ch4[, c("qc_c0", "qc_c0_ratio", "qc_co2_tracer", "qc_co2_slope", "qc_convex",
                            "qc_min_window", "qc_any", "qc_note")]))
```

## The reported row

```{r report}
report <- data.frame(
  UniqueID   = rep_ch4$UniqueID,
  n_obs      = rep_ch4$nb.obs,
  model      = rep_ch4$model,
  CH4_flux_nmol_m2_s = signif(rep_ch4$best.flux, 4),
  CH4_LM_SE  = signif(rep_ch4$LM.SE, 3),
  sigma_ppb  = signif(rep_ch4$sigma_allan, 3),
  MDF        = signif(rep_ch4$MDF, 3),
  MDF_method = rep_ch4$MDF_method,
  detected   = rep_ch4$detected,
  class      = rep_ch4$det_class,
  CO2_flux_umol_m2_s = signif(best_co2$best.flux, 4),
  qc_any     = rep_ch4$qc_any)
t(report)
```

The same row comes out of the one-call wrapper:

```{r wrapper}
invisible(capture.output(       # goFlux's progress bar is captured
  res <- suppressWarnings(process_fluxes(d, gastype = "CH4dry_ppb",
                       precision = c("allan", "mad", "datasheet"),
                       mdf = c("goflux", "wassmann", "christiansen", "two_sigma"),
                       conf = c(0.90, 0.95, 0.99),
                       primary = list(precision = "allan", mdf = "christiansen", conf = 0.95),
                       qc = list(c0 = TRUE, co2_tracer = TRUE, convex = TRUE, min_window = list(secs = 120)),
                       co2 = best_co2))))
res
c(best.flux = res$fluxes$best.flux, MDF = res$fluxes$MDF, method = res$fluxes$MDF_method)
```

## Summary of the numbers

```{r summary, echo = FALSE}
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  quantity = c("observations used", "fit span (s)", "CH4 slope (ppb/s)", "CH4 LM r2",
               "V/A (m)", "P/RT (mol m-3)", "flux.term (mol m-2)",
               "CH4 flux LM (nmol m-2 s-1)", "CH4 flux HM (nmol m-2 s-1)", "CH4 flux reported",
               "sigma CH4 (ppb, Allan)", "MDF goFlux (datasheet)", "MDF Wassmann 95% (allan)",
               "MDF Christiansen 95% (allan)", "MDF 2-sigma (allan)", "reported MDF / method",
               "detected", "CO2 flux (umol m-2 s-1)"),
  value = c(n_used, t_span, signif(slope_ch4, 5), signif(summary(fit_ch4)$r.squared, 4),
            signif(VA, 5), signif(PRT, 5), signif(ft, 5),
            signif(best_ch4$LM.flux, 5), signif(best_ch4$HM.flux, 5), signif(best_ch4$best.flux, 5),
            signif(sigma_ch4, 4), signif(rep_ch4$MDF_goflux_datasheet, 4),
            signif(rep_ch4$MDF_wassmann_allan_95, 4), signif(rep_ch4$MDF_christiansen_allan_95, 4),
            signif(rep_ch4$MDF_two_sigma_allan, 4),
            paste(signif(rep_ch4$MDF, 4), rep_ch4$MDF_method), rep_ch4$det_class,
            signif(best_co2$best.flux, 5))))
```
